claim: The chapter's Speaking Practice NOTES rule (a noun made the topic takes は in place of を or が, and moves to the head of the sentence) appears in two cards but is explained on none.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE NOTES: "When the word that is the topic has the particles が or を, they change to は. When the particle is other than が or を, は is added." and "ばんごはん has been made the topic, so the particle を has changed to は, and ばんごはん comes at the head of the sentence." Cards chan-likes-steak-topic (エマさん、ステーキはすきですか) and supper-before-or-after-meeting (ばんごはんはかいぎのまえにたべますか。あとでたべますか) both ship with no note. No earlier card in the ledger explains を becoming は.
fix: Add a note to chan-likes-steak-topic saying は replaces the が of すき to make steak the topic ('as for steak, do you like it?'), and a note to supper-before-or-after-meeting saying ばんごはんを becomes ばんごはんは and moves to the front for the same reason.
verdictReason: Book ch. 42 SPEAKING PRACTICE NOTES states the rule (が/を become は when the noun is the topic; the topic moves to the head). cards.json: chan-likes-steak-topic and supper-before-or-after-meeting have no note, hint or scene. Ledger: every すき card before Lesson 18 marks the liked thing with が (29 cards), and no earlier note covers を or が becoming は for an object (chapter-13's は-for-known-existence notes are a different case). Learner and Reader saw the same gap from both sides.

claim: GRAMMAR 2's rule that after a verb of movement the second action happens at the place you went is shown on a card with the book's own example, but no back explains it.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "when the first clause uses a verb of movement such as いきます, きます, or かえります, the location of the action of the second clause is assumed to be the same, even if not stated explicitly ... きのう ぎんざに いって、ひるごはんを たべました ... The place where I ate lunch was Ginza." Card went-ginza-ate-lunch: きのうぎんざにいって、ひるごはんをたべました / 'Yesterday I went to Ginza and ate lunch there.' with no note.
fix: Add a note to went-ginza-ate-lunch: after いって (or きて, かえって) the next action is understood to happen at that place, so no で phrase is needed.
verdictReason: Book ch. 42 GRAMMAR 2 states the movement-verb rule and uses this exact sentence as its example. cards.json: went-ginza-ate-lunch has no note, hint or scene; grep of every shipping note in chapter-18 and chapter-18-extras finds nothing about the second action's location (only 'same subject' on ginza-then-meet-friend and 'tense is set by the last verb' on answer-osaka-branch-presentation).

No card in chapter-18 or chapter-18-extras mentions it; the nearest is answer-osaka-branch-presentation's note "The tense is set only by the last verb".

verdictReason: Book ch. 42 GRAMMAR 2 gives the restriction with a statement-plus-suggestion example. No shipping note in either unit mentions mood, tense mismatch, or clauses that cannot be joined (grep of all notes). Polish is the right weight: it is a restriction, not a form to produce.
